title: Metropolitan Police announces exploration of AI to grade and triage child sexual abuse imagery to find unknown victims faster
summary: On 13 Apr 2026 the Met said it is exploring AI to grade and triage child sexual abuse imagery, testing with multiple companies, to flag unknown victims faster; no deployment or outcome yet.
account: The Metropolitan Police Service announced that it is exploring the use of artificial intelligence to support rapid grading and triage of child sexual abuse imagery, so that material possibly relating to unknown victims can be flagged for prioritized safeguarding while reducing officers' manual review of distressing material. The force said it is in conversations with multiple companies and testing how this could work, alongside a separate tool that reviews 641,000 messages in 35 minutes and a £10 million investment in victim interview suites. It cited more than 5,400 child sexual abuse offenses investigated in the past year and over 1,300 children safeguarded. Deputy Commissioner Matt Jukes said speed matters for safeguarding and that human judgment and oversight would remain central. OECD AIM records it as an 'AI hazard' (2026-04-13-83b8), noting the use is under consideration and not implemented.
purpose: Rapidly analyze seized imagery to grade it (categories A to C) and flag content possibly showing previously unknown victims, prioritizing safeguarding and reducing officer exposure.
system: Unnamed AI grading and triage tools under evaluation
domain: Child protection / online child sexual abuse investigation
taxonomy_note: An announcement of exploration, not a deployment: no event, no outcome, all depths null. OECD AIM labels it an 'AI hazard'.
